_comment: Expectation manifest for this skill's frozen acceptance-checks.
Enforced repo-wide by scripts/evals-all.mjs on every push and PR.
expect "green" = a past fix that must not regress. MUST exit 0.
expect "red"   = a known-failing check (open concern / in-flight item). MUST exit 0 or 1;
>=2 is harness rot (it failed to RUN). A red check that turns GREEN does NOT
fail the gate -- it prints a promote-me notice; move it to green when its fix lands.
A check file missing from this manifest FAILS the gate: an unlisted check is an unguarded check.
LOCKED (evals/**): improvement loops may never edit this file -- otherwise a loop could flip a
regressing check to "red" and escape its own fence.

autofix-bounded.note: Added 2026-08-03; re-axed 2026-09-21 (gate on fix class, not REFUTED status); rewritten 2026-10-26. The sibling `<plan>.autofix.md` was a second copy of the plan the reader had to diff by hand while git already held the original, and the 're-run steps 3-6 per fix' ritual re-verified transcriptions against the evidence that had just determined them. The rule 'a NO-GO whose refutations all need a decision does not move' froze a verdict even after the human decided and the fix landed. Now: edit in place, never choose a needs-decision repair for the human, re-adjudicate each fixed row against the evidence that settled it, and the verdict is whatever validate.mjs derives from the rows.

mutations.find: 10. **Offer autofix — never automatic.**

mutations.why: reintroduces the sibling copy instead of an in-place edit
mutations.find:
Edit the plan file **in place** — git is the record, so
    say so first if it is untracked or dirty;

mutations.why: removes the bullet that stops autofix choosing a new approach for the human -- the worst blast radius
mutations.find:
- **A `REFUTED` row whose repair needs a new approach** — the plan's model of reality is
  wrong and the evidence does not say what to do instead. Choosing that is design. Autofix
  must not choose it, and must not let the plan read as if it had.

mutations.why: collapses the gate back onto the REFUTED status
mutations.find:
The gate is the **fix class**, never the status. `REFUTED` is not the line: a claim can be
refuted by evidence that also fully determines its correction (the symbol moved; the target
does not exist), and transcribing that is not a decision.

mutations.why: freezes the verdict after a fix -- the 'NO-GO never moves' rule
mutations.find: No verdict is frozen, and none moves without a row that moved first.
mutations.replace: A NO-GO does not move after autofix, and must not be made to.

After editing, re-adjudicate each fixed row against the evidence that settled it — the
Makefile that has `test`, the human's answer — update its status and cite that evidence, then
re-run `validate.mjs`.

goal-coverage.note: Added 2026-08-03. plan-check had NO concept of the plan's goal -- on 9c86ced the only /goal/i match across SKILL.md, template.html and both references was incidental prose. It fell out of the skill's own framing: step 2 keeps only 'atomic checkable propositions' and a goal has no truth value, so it never survived decomposition. Cost: the DoD was unanchored (every criterion checkable, none of them achieving the objective, and the report blind to it), GO meant 'the claims hold' rather than 'this plan achieves its goal', and lirbox:conductor seeds its DoDGate from #dod so it verified faithfully toward a target nobody validated. Guards BOTH halves deliberately -- a goal line without the adjudication is decoration, and decoration is exactly what measured no-better last time.

mutations.find: Goal: {{PLAN_GOAL}}

mutations.why: makes the goal-coverage row optional, which is the same as absent -- the adjudication is the half that catches a plan solving the wrong problem
mutations.find: const goalRows = rows.filter((tag) => attr(tag, 'data-goal-coverage') !== null);

mutations.why: removes the SKILL.md instruction tying the DoD back to the goal, leaving the validator to demand a row nothing tells the model to produce

*if every
   DoD criterion were met, would the stated goal be achieved?*

fix-disposition.note: Added 2026-08-05. SKILL.md step 7 has demanded a `fix:` disposition on every open row since #57 and the model largely ignored it: MEASURED at 4/10 in BOTH arms of a 20-trial paired Harbor run on execution-shape (2026-08-04), with a LENIENT grader that scored 1 for a single `fix:` string anywhere in the file -- six of ten reports per arm had none at all, in runs whose reports carried 6-12 open rows each. Every other element of the same contract sat at ~100% over the same runs (#dod 10/10, id=goal 20/20, data-goal-coverage 20/20, #taskgraph 10/10). The one thing they share and this lacked: a template slot and a validate.mjs rule. SKILL.md step 9 loops the model until validate.mjs exits 0, so a rule living only in prose never enters the loop. Guards the invariant PER ROW on purpose -- a file-level `fix:` grep is the exact leniency the Harbor grader had, and it lets one tagged row excuse ten untagged ones. 2026-10-26: widened to every non-VERIFIED row (UNSTATED-ASSUMPTION is now open); the REFUTED exemption mutation is gone because the row loop no longer has a separate tag set.

mutations.why: removes the disposition slot from the claim-row specimen, so nothing reaches the model at the moment it writes the HTML -- the precise gap that measured 4/10

mutations.why: removes the validator rule entirely, putting the convention back in prose-only territory

mutations.find: const FIX = /\bfix:\s*(mechanical|needs-decision)\b/i;

execution-shape.note: Added 2026-08-03. plan-check verified whether a plan was CORRECT but never whether its declared task graph was HONEST -- and an agentic runner dispatches from those declarations literally, so an undeclared edge runs concurrently what must not be. Found in two plans plan-check had itself reviewed: a task declaring 'Consumes: nothing' whose own step 6 said 'run it after Task 1 has landed', and one function claimed by five of eight tasks with no task declaring the overlap. Guards the invariant that the declared graph is tested against the file-level truth the plan itself states -- NOT that the plan be parallel. Parallelism is an output of an honest graph; asking for it directly produces a plan claiming independence it does not have. 2026-10-26: the #taskgraph block and its task-graph check were removed -- nothing in the repo consumed it (the conductor that dispatched DAGs is gone). The collision and undeclared-edge findings remain as claim rows.

- **A file claimed by more than one task** — a collision, but classify it before you serialize

  cost at integration, not an ordering constraint — recording it as a dependency serializes
  work that has none. Say which runner you assumed; an unclassified collision is the finding.

- **Undeclared dependency edges** — stated in step prose, absent from the task's own
  dependency block. The block is what a runner reads. `UNSTATED-ASSUMPTION`.

verdict-by-fix-class.note: Added 2026-10-26. SKILL.md said NO-GO on a REFUTED 'critical path' while validate.mjs forced NO-GO on ANY refutation, so a wrong Makefile target blocked a whole plan and autofix grew a re-verification ritual to walk the typo back. UNSTATED-ASSUMPTION was not open at all. Now: REFUTED + needs-decision is NO-GO; REFUTED + mechanical and UNSTATED-ASSUMPTION are conditions.

go-reachable.note: Added 2026-10-26. A mandatory blind-spot pass + every BLIND-SPOT-RISK open made GO unreachable once generic risks were listed; the interview gate demanded every askable open row be asked while interrogation.md said to drop non-verdict-changing questions. Now blind spots are plan-specific and the gate blocks only on verdict-changing questions.

`BLIND-SPOT-RISK` row — specific to this plan, with the reason it applies. A risk that would
apply to every plan ("what if the network fails?") is not a finding; it is noise that buries one.
